description: The ophys module on synthetic recordings with known shifts and cells: SciScan raw, TIFF and multi-ROI ScanImage files are read, the data variables are set up by the module's tool, and motion correction, image statistics (a computed fragment), ROI detection (the correlation image, and Quicky's), signal extraction (also with the neuropil in slices around each ROI, dev's neuropil grown at most maxNeuropilRadius steps, and every channel in one run, each ROI's signal from its own channel), ΔF/F, deconvolution (AR(1) and dev's default AR(2)), denoising, downsampling, aligning sessions, ROI curation, the viewer's frames and projections (std, local correlation and dev's Mean CLAHE), the Detect tool in dev's five autodetection modes (rois.detect mode), a method previewed on the first frames (writing nothing), methods run on frames firstFrame..lastFrame only (also in a preview, which takes the first frames of that range), every plane of a two-plane recording processed in one run (plane 0: the aligned planes in one stack, the projections a frame per plane, the ROIs of both planes in one file with their places, and the signals of each ROI from its own plane), the recordings' frame rate, pixel size and z step read from their files (data.frame's metadata) and written into the session's columns by ophys.read_metadata, and the brain region at a FOV's position give the values of the ground truth, which make_data.py computes from the scenes directly (the AR(1) deconvolution with a general optimiser, the AR(2) one, which OASIS solves greedily, by that greedy method written out plainly). The module's dashboard page and its atlas are served by app.plugins and modules.resource; the FOV map's injection sites are kept with modules.saveData, as JSON text given back exactly. ROIs of another variable or of a JSON file are imported into an ROI variable (rois.update import: replace, append, or append those that do not overlap, as roimanager adds loaded ROIs; also at a plane), and a method is previewed on one ROI's column of the signals, its one-column outputs given as traces (the deconvolution explorer). An ROI's neuropil is given as signal extraction takes it (rois.neuropil, worked out by hand on single-pixel ROIs: a ring at a square distance, or dev's expansion, also in slices or grown a few steps at most, among the ROIs not rejected, with the options given or those of a method's preset or preferred preset).
